title: Passage from finite Galois coordinates to the profinite Cech nerve and its faces
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\Omega/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(\Omega)$ with its Krull topology. For each finite Galois intermediate field $E$ put $Q_E=\operatorname{Aut}_k(E)$. Assume the maps
$$\theta_{E,q}:\Omega\otimes_k E^{\otimes_k q}\longrightarrow\Omega^{Q_E^q},\quad (a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_q)(g_1,\ldots,g_q)=a_0g_1(a_1)\cdots(g_1\cdots g_q)(a_q)$$
are $\Omega$-algebra isomorphisms compatible with inclusions of $E$ and restriction of automorphisms, for all $q\geq0$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Write $\Omega[G^q]=\varprojlim_E\coprod_{Q_E^q}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, equivalently the profinite test object of [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. There are canonical identifications
$$\Omega^{\otimes_k(q+1)}\cong\varinjlim_E\Omega^{Q_E^q}\cong LC(G^q,\Omega),\qquad W_q:=(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)^{q+1}_{/k}\cong\Omega[G^q],$$
where $LC$ denotes locally constant functions with pointwise operations and the first tensor factor gives the structure over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Every continuous map from $G^q$ to a finite discrete set factors through some $Q_E^q$. Write group multiplication as composition of field automorphisms: $(gh)(a)=g(h(a))$. The following coordinate convention specifies the vertices and all faces, including the change of base vertex. On a component labelled $(g_1,\ldots,g_q)\in G^q$, and for a ring-valued base point $x:\Omega\to B$, the vertices are the ring maps
$$x,\quad x\circ g_1,\quad x\circ(g_1g_2),\quad\ldots,\quad x\circ(g_1\cdots g_q).$$
Thus $xg:=x\circ g$ on ring maps; on scheme-valued points $t:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ this means $tg=\operatorname{Spec}(g)\circ t$. For $q\geq1$, deleting vertex zero replaces the base point by $xg_1$ and drops $g_1$; deleting vertex $i$, $0<i<q$, replaces $(g_i,g_{i+1})$ by $g_ig_{i+1}$; deleting vertex $q$ drops $g_q$. On coordinate rings the first face is the $k$-algebra map
$$d_0^*:LC(G^{q-1},\Omega)\longrightarrow LC(G^q,\Omega),\qquad (d_0^*f)(g_1,\ldots,g_q)=g_1\bigl(f(g_2,\ldots,g_q)\bigr).$$
The other faces are precomposition with the displayed increment maps. Repeating vertex $i$, $0\leq i\leq q$, inserts $1$ after the first $i$ increments. These formulas specify scheme morphisms, not merely maps on points. For an identification $\varepsilon_{01}$ from vertex 1 to vertex 0, the descent cocycle convention is $\varepsilon_{02}=\varepsilon_{01}\circ\varepsilon_{12}$, with each identification pulled back to the triple overlap. In a constant coefficient fibre trivialization, where the base-vertex change acts trivially on the coefficient values, this reads $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$; without that triviality the pullback along the moved base vertex is retained.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], $\Omega/k$ is Galois. Apply [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit]: the finite Galois intermediate fields form a nonempty directed set $I$, and restriction identifies $G$ with $\varprojlim_E Q_E$ as a profinite group. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] every finite subset of $\Omega$ lies in one $E$, so $\Omega$ is their directed union. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends], every automorphism of $E$ extends to $\Omega$: both extensions over $k$ are normal. Hence $G\to Q_E$ and its $q$-fold product are surjective. Taking the group-limit coordinates in each of the $q$ positions gives $G^q=\varprojlim_E Q_E^q$ as profinite spaces: a compatible family gives one element of $G$ in each position, and both this correspondence and its inverse are continuous by the coordinate topology. For $q=0$ this is the singleton system.

Put $B_{E,q}=\Omega\otimes_k E^{\otimes_k q}$ and $T_q=\Omega^{\otimes_k(q+1)}$. Their natural maps exhibit $T_q=\varinjlim_E B_{E,q}$ as $\Omega$-algebras. Here is the universal property explicitly. Given a compatible cocone $f_E:B_{E,q}\to C$ into a commutative $\Omega$-algebra, for $1\leq j\leq q$ send $a\in\Omega$ to $f_E(1\otimes\cdots\otimes a\otimes\cdots\otimes1)$ with $a$ in slot $j$, choosing $E$ containing $a$. A common upper stage makes this independent of the choice. Taking a stage containing $a,b$ verifies addition and multiplication, so these are $k$-algebra maps $\Omega\to C$. Together with the specified zeroth map they extend uniquely to $T_q\to C$ by the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The extension agrees with every $f_E$ on every tensor factor, hence on $B_{E,q}$; the same factorwise uniqueness proves uniqueness on $T_q$. The assumed compatible $\theta_{E,q}$ therefore give $T_q\cong\varinjlim_E\Omega^{Q_E^q}$. At $q=0$ all maps are the identity of $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits), explicit universal-property argument using common finite stages; algebra tensor universal property as in schemes.tex Tag 01I4.

proof.text: Pullback along $G^q\to Q_E^q$ defines compatible $\Omega$-algebra maps $\Omega^{Q_E^q}\to LC(G^q,\Omega)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-limit-function-factorization] to the small cofiltered diagram $E\mapsto Q_E^q$ and the limiting cone from step 1. Every locally constant $\Omega$-valued function is the pullback of a function on one finite stage, so the induced map from the colimit is surjective. If two finite-stage functions have the same pullback, pass to a common upper stage $E''$; surjectivity of $G^q\to Q_{E''}^q$ implies their pullbacks on that stage are equal. This proves injectivity and hence the claimed ring identification. A continuous map to a finite discrete set is locally constant, so the very same cited factorization, with that set as codomain, proves the finite-map clause. In particular each finite quotient partition of $G^q$ is refined by a $Q_E^q$-partition.

Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $W_q$ with $\operatorname{Spec}T_q$, with its $j$-th projection induced by the $j$-th tensor inclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit], the colimit of step 2 makes this spectrum the scheme limit of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega^{Q_E^q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] each stage is the disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ indexed by $Q_E^q$, with the stated evaluation projections. The transitions are those induced by restriction, because the $\theta_{E,q}$ are compatible by hypothesis. This is exactly the inverse limit defining $\Omega[G^q]$. It agrees with [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]: step 3 shows that these partitions refine every finite quotient partition, and a cone over these stages extends uniquely to any finite quotient by choosing a refinement; two choices agree after a common upper stage. Thus the limits have the same universal property. All comparison maps preserve the zeroth tensor inclusion, so this is an identification over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$.

proof.text: For $a\in\Omega$ choose a finite Galois $E$ containing it and evaluate the assumed formula on the tensor with $a$ in slot $j$ and $1$ elsewhere. The resulting vertex coordinate is $a\mapsto(g_1\cdots g_j)(a)$, with the empty product for $j=0$. At a ring-valued base point $x:\Omega\to B$, composition gives $x\circ(g_1\cdots g_j)$. Contravariance of $\operatorname{Spec}$ turns this into $\operatorname{Spec}(g_1\cdots g_j)\circ t$ on scheme-valued base points $t$, explaining the precise order in the corrected statement. This is equality of the projection ring homomorphisms from step 4, using the tensor-factor uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], rather than an inference from geometric points alone.

proof.text:
Deleting vertex $i$ pulls a pure tensor in $T_{q-1}$ back to the tensor in $T_q$ with $1$ inserted in slot $i$. For $i=0$, evaluating gives
$$g_1(a_0)(g_1g_2)(a_1)\cdots(g_1\cdots g_q)(a_{q-1})=g_1\bigl(a_0g_2(a_1)\cdots(g_2\cdots g_q)(a_{q-1})\bigr).$$
This is exactly the stated $d_0^*$, with the new base map $x\circ g_1$. For $0<i<q$, inserting $1$ discards the $i$-th cumulative product; the increments between the retained vertices are $g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_q$. Inserting $1$ last simply drops $g_q$. These equalities on tensor factors determine the ring homomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], and hence the scheme morphisms. To check that the first formula sends locally constant functions to locally constant functions, write any such function at stage $E$ by step 3; its finite list of values lies in a finite Galois $E'$ by step 1. The formula then depends only on restrictions of all increments to a common upper field of $E,E'$. Thus it too is locally constant. In degree one the two faces on constants $a\in\Omega$ are $a\mapsto(g\mapsto g(a))$ and $a\mapsto(g\mapsto a)$; the first is a $k$-algebra map, generally not an $\Omega$-algebra map.

proof.text: Repeating vertex $i$ pulls a tensor in $T_{q+1}$ back by multiplying the entries in slots $i,i+1$. Under evaluation this repeats the $i$-th cumulative product, so its increments are $g_1,\ldots,g_i,1,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_q$. Equality follows directly from $p(a_i a_{i+1})=p(a_i)p(a_{i+1})$ for the cumulative automorphism $p=g_1\cdots g_i$. Tensor-factor uniqueness [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] again proves equality of ring maps. This includes $i=0$ and $i=q$; for $q=0$ the diagonal inserts the single increment $1$. Faces and degeneracies are the actual vertex deletions and repetitions, so their simplicial identities are inherited from those operations.

proof.text: On a triple the vertex labels are $(x,xg,xgh)$. Its three edge labels, with their bases, are $(x,g)$ for $01$, $(xg,h)$ for $12$, and $(x,gh)$ for $02$. An identification from the later fibre to the earlier fibre composes as $\varepsilon_{02}=\varepsilon_{01}\circ\varepsilon_{12}$ by the definition of the descent cocycle written in the statement. Thus the order is first the $h$ arrow and then the $g$ arrow. In constant coefficient fibre coordinates the two matrices or automorphisms are $c(g),c(h)$, giving $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$. Generally the $12$ identification is pulled back along the moved base; for structure-ring matrix coefficients its value is $g(c(h))$, and the equation is $c(gh)=c(g)g(c(h))$. This explains why the coefficient action cannot be silently dropped, while giving exactly the untwisted convention used for constant coefficients by the parent item.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q45-0d92ddac3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the delivery in full: one commit containing the item and the Q45 report, no new nodes, no repair note (so the re-split rule does not apply); the base item was unsplit with no proof. Two statement changes, both named in the report and neither a weakening. (1) The base's '$xg$ = precompose by $\operatorname{Spec}g$' becomes the ring-point convention $xg=x\circ g$, $tg=\operatorname{Spec}(g)\circ t$. Checked with $\theta$: the j-th projection ring map is $a\mapsto(g_1\cdots g_j)(a)$, so the cumulative vertex labels are unchanged. (2) The base's undefined '$c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$' becomes $\varepsilon_{02}=\varepsilon_{01}\circ\varepsilon_{12}$, with the untwisted form for constant coefficient fibres. The twist is real: for $\mathbb R\subset\mathbb C$, $d_0^*a=(g\mapsto g(a))$ but $d_1^*a=(g\mapsto a)$. The parent lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates is still correct: its $R_A$ coefficients have a trivial base-vertex action by lem-sfb-galois-continuous-section-naturality (its step 3). Maintainer note: the parent's step 2 should say 'in constant coefficient fibres'. Checked every cited statement: the Krull limit needs Galois (from separable-closure-exists-galois (2)); normal-subextension extension needs $\Omega/k$ and $E/k$ normal; the factorization leaf needs a small cofiltered diagram in Prof, any set A, locally constant h; fibre product, Spec colimit-limit, finite coproduct; def-sfb-profinite-test-objects $X[S]=\lim\coprod_{S_i}X$, with cofinality written out. All proof citations are Mathlib leaves or definitions, so no tool_uses are needed. Recomputed face 0 ($g_1(f(g_2,\dots))$), interior faces ($g_ig_{i+1}$), the last face, degeneracies (inserted 1, $p(a_ia_{i+1})$) and the cocycle with base $xg$ on edge 12. Small cases: q=0, G=1, $\mathbb R\subset\mathbb C$, $S_3$ order. Duplicates: the pointed-limit-cover Čech nodes concern a different object (a limit T over general X, with $\pi_1$, and no ring formulas or semilinear $d_0^*$), so they do not duplicate the item. Stacks 0BU2 and 00DD read at the cited labels; no SGA. Details in review.md.
